title: Who’s Marketing Better? Rhone or Ten Thousand? ⛹🏻
description: Who’s Marketing Better? Rhone or Ten Thousand? ⛹🏻
transcript: Whose marketing is better, Rone or 10,000? Both brands are running around 120 meta ads. So this isn't about volume, it's about how they convert attention into revenue. Rone sends traffic straight to the product page. 10,000 sends traffic to the collection page. Rone chooses a faster path with higher intent and more direct conversions. But here's where it gets interesting. Ten Thousand's collection flow isn't a weakness, it's a brand play. They're letting customers explore multiple products and multiple entry points. This has a higher chance to find the perfect fit, and it can actually increase their AOVs if the experience is dialed. Now layer in retail. Rome has 20+ stores. 10,000 has zero. The Rone has a physical presence. Trust is built offline, which absolutely helps online conversions. But 10,000, they're fully digital, which means every dollar is forced to perform. No retail safety net. Different game, and it's definitely different pressure. Now look at creative strategy. Rome leans into their performance with UDC. Offers direct response, fast conversions. 10,000 leans into their brand with clean visuals, premium positioning, and less aggressive marketing and more controlled perception around who they are. So what's actually happening here? Rone is optimizing for immediate revenue. 10,000 is optimizing for long term brand equity. So who do you think is winning? Let me know below.
